evidence: The deposition took place at 200 ◦C using trimethylaluminium [Al(CH3)3] and water as the aluminium and oxygen source, respectively. Each cycle consisted of a 1.3 s precursor pulse, 20 s exposition time and 60 s purging time with Ar. ... The thickness of the Al2O3 shell is controlled by the number of precursor/purge cycles. In our study, a total number of 65 cycles was used, which gives an alumina thickness of 10.0 ± 0.3 nm as measured from TEM images.
